overall: The AG found the committee may keep withholding redacted 2014 collective bargaining executive session minutes for now, and that approving the CBA by vote in executive session was lawful. No violation found.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee improperly redacted portions of 17 sets of 2014 executive session minutes on collective bargaining strategy with a teachers' union.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee may continue to withhold the redacted portions of the 17 sets of executive session minutes concerning the Committee's 2014 collective bargaining discussions with Unit A.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee's June 2014 vote to approve a collective bargaining agreement should have been taken in open session rather than executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Because public disclosure of the vote at that time had the potential to detrimentally affect both the Committee's bargaining and litigating positions, we find that this action was lawful.

remedy: Committee must periodically review the withheld executive session minutes and release them at some time in the future, and is encouraged to review them after the next bargaining cycle.
remedy_passage: However, it must periodically review the minutes, and will have to release them at some time in the future.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
